done.why: I reached the Carousel Room, a disorienting maze-like spot, and stopped. I had seen the main ideas and nothing pulled me further.

about: A Zork-flavoured cave crawl. You start in a barrow with a lamp and an Elvish sword, cross a ravine and explore caverns and a formal garden. A Wizard keeps appearing and casting spells on you. His spells make illusory objects, make your sword glow, and make you drop things.

moments.note: Attacking the bridge with the sword made the Wizard appear. His speech about treasure south of the ravine was a nice touch.
The jewels were an illusion. The refusal line explained it wittily, and the room 'looks embarrassed'.
The room reverted to normal once I tried to read the fake Zork copy.
Odd phrasings such as 'politely ask the lantern to take me' got only 'That sentence isn't one I recognize.'
The Wizard's spell made me drop the lamp while I was reading the newspaper.

wished: Wear or use the illusory items in some way.
Do something more with the unicorn.

lines.line: Your hand closes on nothing, and your eye on less. It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Funny, and it showed how the Wizard's magic works.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you.
lines.why: Characterful Wizard that sets the goal.

fun.why: The illusion gimmick and the Wizard's visits were charming. I explored only briefly and had no puzzle to solve.

engagement.why: Interested at first, but I found no strong thread to follow in about 27 turns.

difficulty.why: I met no real obstacles in the stretch I played.

interestingness.why: Blending a Zork homage with a Wizard who conjures fake objects is a good idea.

prose.why: Witty, with polished custom lines mixed with classic Zork text.
